book.title: Calista's Paradox
book.subtitle: A magical realist leadership fable told in three nights
book.description: Calista inherits a failing gemstone business and thinks the challenge will be survival: buyers, bills, and the brutal standards of master jewelers who miss nothing. Then she is handed an emerald commission that could make her name, and the verdict lands like a sentence: none of her stones are good enough. As pressure tightens around the atelier, a mysterious Consultant draws her into a realm he calls LEGACY, where every lesson feels like a test of ethics, ambition, and agency, and the consequences can be mortal. Told over three nights and framed as 100 lessons, Calista's Paradox blends craft realism, cosmopolitan grit, and quiet mysticism into a story about inheritance, responsibility, and the cost of becoming someone worth trusting.
book.author: Erik Åkesson and Elaine Stirling

audienceMatch.title: Audience Match
audienceMatch.engagement: High discussion engagement; medium-to-high completion supported by an episodic, lesson-based structure and strong audio appeal.
audienceMatch.keyCharacteristics: This fits upmarket adult readers who like literary commercial fiction with a clear organizing concept, moral pressure instead of chase pacing, and a slightly mystical edge that stays emotionally logical. The core readership skews 30 to 55 and is globally English language, college educated to postgraduate, with a strong overlap among book club readers, culture forward creatives, and professionals drawn to stories about leadership, burnout, reinvention, and integrity. They respond quickly when the book is pitched as story first with a “lessons” experience, especially when paired with tactile, high status craft stakes like gemstones, sourcing, and mastery.
audienceMatch.detailedAnalysis: Discovery tends to cluster around Instagram and TikTok for quotable lesson snippets and gemstone visuals, LinkedIn and leadership adjacent podcasts for the fable framing, and independent bookstores, newsletters, and reading groups for credibility and conversation value. Format preferences lean ebook and audiobook, which matches the first person, conversational narrator voice and the three night structure that is easy to sample, share, and discuss in segments.

analysisOverview.title: Analysis Overview
analysisOverview.readership: The primary audience is an established, globally minded upmarket cohort with a meaningful professional segment across consulting, marketing, design, product, and adjacent fields, plus a secondary, younger digital first group that values stylish packaging, shareable lines, and modern meaning making without preachiness. Together they form a sizable English language market with strong word of mouth potential through book clubs, podcasts, and algorithmic read alike pathways anchored to philosophical, allegorical fiction.
analysisOverview.classification: Position this in adult upmarket literary commercial fiction as a philosophical fable with magical realist stakes, grounded in artisan jewelry craft and business ethics rather than spectacle. The comps and category signals point to readers who enjoy allegorical, lesson-forward narratives with accessible prose and a structured transformation arc, while the emerald trial and atelier authenticity deliver a distinctive, visual engine. Genre signals in the report are organized using a bespoke taxonomy of subgenres, which supports pitching the book’s themes and readership pull without forcing it into a single shelf.
analysisOverview.personas: The primary persona, Nadia Petrova, is the clearest commercial heartbeat: a culture forward, book club active reader who wants fiction that feels beautiful and useful, with ethical dilemmas, craft detail, and a memorable organizing concept she can discuss and quote. She signals a readership that values aesthetic precision, moral coherence, and reflective payoff, and that will recommend when the voice stays wry and earned rather than didactic. The secondary persona, Marcus Alvarez, widens reach into midlife professional readers who prefer psychologically literate, framework friendly storytelling and may share crisp takeaways in leadership oriented circles.
analysisOverview.marketingGuidance: Use the marketing insights to build early campaigns around repeatable hooks and visuals: emeralds under a loupe, a canal side jewelry shop, and a solitary Consultant voice framing LEGACY as both gift and trap, then sequence creative from lesson teasers to excerpt proof to retailer conversion. Copy that tends to win is specific and talkable, such as “a story told in three nights,” “100 lessons on leadership and legacy,” and the emerald verdict line, while creative hooks should emphasize craft, ethics, and consequence without selling it as nonfiction. This marketing layer will expand into its own product over time, but it is currently included as part of the first report so the report holder can shape initial testing with cohesive messaging, lead magnets, and launch ready assets.

positioning.title: Market Positioning: Upmarket Philosophical Fable with Magical-Realist Stakes
positioning.subtitle: A contemporary leadership-and-legacy allegory grounded in artisan jewellery craft and a midlife narrator’s wry self-reckoning
positioning.description: Calista’s Paradox sits in the upmarket lane between literary-commercial fiction and philosophical fable, using a first-person, conversational consultant narrator to braid practical business pressure (a failing wholesale gemstone firm; the emerald trial for a high-profile commission) with a supernatural instructional framework (LEGACY; “100 Lessons,” “told in 3 nights”). The book’s appeal comes from its accessible, modern voice and cosmopolitan setting, paired with allegorical, moral-testing mechanics reminiscent of guided-lesson classics. The jewellery atelier detail and ethics-of-craft focus create a distinctive, tactile engine for the themes of inheritance, responsibility, fate versus agency, and renewal—positioning it for book-club readers, literary-fable fans, and professionals attracted to narrative leadership parables.

moodAndTone.title: Mood & Tone
moodAndTone.subtitle: Reflective, wry, mildly melancholic—shot through with quiet mysticism and moral urgency
moodAndTone.description: The dominant mood is contemplative and slightly bittersweet, with dry, sardonic humor tempering high personal stakes. The narrative voice (a 47-year-old, twice-divorced consultant) delivers intimate, self-aware observation—often philosophical, occasionally sensual, but not erotic-forward—while the atmosphere alternates between grounded urban interiors (workbench, bar, canal town streets) and brief, uncanny intrusions tied to LEGACY. Tension comes less from action pacing and more from moral pressure: craftsmanship judged by master jewellers, business survival on the line, and a metaphysical system whose lessons can “kill or renew.” The emotional aftertaste trends reflective and mildly uplifting, leaning into intellectual engagement and curiosity rather than catharsis-heavy drama.

marketing.title: Calista’s Paradox: Stage 1 Global Launch Marketing Plan
marketing.subtitle: A literary-commercial, magical-realist leadership fable positioned for book clubs, upmarket fiction readers, and professional audiences
marketing.objective: Drive broad awareness and qualified demand for Calista’s Paradox by positioning it as an upmarket philosophical fable (“100 Lessons on Leadership & Legacy”) with strong visual craft hooks (jewellery/emeralds) and book-club/podcast suitability, converting interest into pre-orders, first-30-day sales velocity, and sustained discovery.
marketing.keyInsight: Readers who enjoy reflective, allegorical fiction (Coelho/Dickens/Gaarder comps) will engage faster when the book is framed as both a story and a practical “lessons” experience—especially when paired with highly visual artisan stakes (emerald trial) and a midlife, wry narrator voice that signals maturity, relevance, and discussion value.
howToUse: Use the Messaging Framework to keep every asset anchored to: (1) 100 Lessons/3 nights, (2) legacy as gift/trap, (3) craft + ethics + leadership, (4) mysterious guide with life-or-death consequences.
Build creative around three repeatable visual motifs: emeralds under a loupe, canal-side jewellery shop, a solitary consultant at a bar (reflection/voice).
Sequence content by funnel: teasers of “Lessons” for awareness, excerpt-led proof for consideration, and retailer-specific CTAs + social proof for conversion.

Run parallel tracks: (A) reader-facing literary/magical-realism marketing and (B) professional-facing leadership-fable marketing (LinkedIn, business podcasts) without over-promising nonfiction utility.
Localize ads by English language first, then expand to high-readership markets with global/cosmopolitan resonance (UK/IE, CA, AU/NZ, EU English readers, India, Singapore).
primaryKPIs: Pre-orders (weekly) and pre-order conversion rate from landing page
First 30-day unit sales and sell-through by format (ebook/print/audio)
Email list growth (net new subscribers) and welcome-sequence CTR
Retail page conversion rate (Amazon/Apple/Google/Kobo) and add-to-cart rate
Cost per email subscriber (paid social) and cost per purchase (ROAS/CPA)
Audio sample plays and audiobook trial conversions (where available)
Press/podcast bookings secured and episode download totals
Book club kit downloads and book club inquiries

campaignStructure.title: Three-Funnel Structure: Lessons-First Discovery to Retail Conversion

funnels.name: Awareness
funnels.description: Introduce the concept: a magical-realist, philosophical fable told in three nights, framed as 100 lessons, with jewellery-craft stakes and a wry midlife narrator.
funnels.formats: Short-form video (15–30s), static image ads (emerald/loupe/shop), quote cards (“Legacy is both gift and trap.”), teaser carousel (3 nights / 3 questions), podcast pitch one-sheet, influencer seeding to bookstagram/booktok (upmarket/literary).
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for reach and video views; test 6–10 hooks (Legacy/100 Lessons/emerald trial/mysterious Consultant/book-club debate prompt). Rotate creatives weekly; prioritize highest save/share rate as indicator of book-club resonance.

funnels.name: Consideration
funnels.description: Provide proof of tone and content: sample chapter/excerpt, “5 of the 100 Lessons” lead magnet, comps positioning, and craftsmanship detail to build trust and intent.
funnels.formats: Lead-gen ads to a landing page, email capture with downloadable Book Club Kit + discussion questions, author/narrator voice audio snippet, longer video (45–60s) with “What is LEGACY?” framing, LinkedIn article series excerpting lessons (as fiction quotes).
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for landing-page views and email sign-ups; A/B test lead magnets (Book Club Kit vs. ‘5 Lessons’). Retarget engagers with excerpt-based creatives; prioritize CTR and subscriber-to-preorder conversion.

funnels.name: Conversion
funnels.description: Turn intent into purchases across formats with clear retailer CTAs, urgency windows (pre-order bonuses/launch week), and social proof (reviews, podcast features, book club endorsements).
funnels.formats: Retargeting ads (dynamic creative), retailer-link hub, preorder bonus (limited-time: signed bookplate/bonus chapter/‘Lesson cards’ PDF), launch-week email sequence, Goodreads/StoryGraph giveaways, Amazon/BookBub ads, audio-first creatives for Audible/Spotify where applicable.
funnels.optimisation: Optimize for purchases/ROAS; segment retargeting (video viewers, site visitors, email clickers). Suppress recent purchasers; shift budget to best-performing retailer/format by geography.

budgetAllocation.title: Stage 1 Budget Allocation (Percentage-Based)
budgetAllocation.breakdown: Paid social (Meta/IG/FB): 35%; Retail ads (Amazon/BookBub/Apple/Kobo): 25%; Content production (video, graphics, landing page): 15%; PR/podcasts/newsletters (pitching tools, services, press materials): 10%; Influencer/bookstagram seeding + ARC logistics: 5%; Giveaways (Goodreads/StoryGraph) + book club kit assets: 5%; Testing/contingency: 5%.

flightSchedule.title: Recommended Flight Schedule (10–12 Weeks Total)
flightSchedule.timeline: Weeks -8 to -6: Platform setup (landing page, retailer links, pixel, email automations), ARC outreach, creative production. Weeks -6 to -4: Awareness burst (video views/reach) + begin podcast/newsletter pitching. Weeks -4 to -2: Consideration push (lead magnet + excerpt) + book club kit launch + influencer seeding. Weeks -2 to Launch: Conversion ramp (retargeting, preorder CTA, giveaways). Launch Week: Highest spend on conversion + social proof amplification. Weeks +1 to +4: Sustain (retargeting, review capture, podcast drops, book club programming, retailer ad optimization).

messagingFramework.title: Positioning and Message Pillars
messagingFramework.primaryTagline: Legacy is both gift and trap—one must be opened, the other escaped.
supportingMessages: A young jewellery designer inherits a failing gemstone business—and an impossible emerald test.
A mysterious Consultant guides her through LEGACY: a realm of lessons where consequences can be mortal.
A magical-realist fable told over three nights, framed as 100 lessons on leadership and responsibility.
Upmarket, wry, and reflective—built for readers who like stories that leave you thinking.
Craftsmanship, ethics, and ambition collide in a cosmopolitan European setting with global echoes.

romanceReaders.title: For Romance-Adjacent Readers (Low Heat, High Emotion)
romanceReaders.message: If you like emotionally intelligent, sensual atmosphere without explicit scenes, Calista’s Paradox offers intimate tension in a story driven by moral choice, mentorship, and personal renewal—more aching than steamy.

bookClubs.title: For Book Clubs
bookClubs.message: A discussion-ready fable about legacy, ambition, and ethical craft—structured in ‘three nights’ and ‘100 lessons’ with clear debate prompts: Is legacy a burden or a gift? Who gets to judge quality and worth? What does a life reset actually cost?

matureReaders.title: For Mature Readers (Midlife Lens)
matureReaders.message: A wry, first-person narrator confronts stagnation, health, and meaning—while guiding a younger protagonist through high-stakes tests. A thoughtful read about reinvention when the old story no longer fits.

ruralReaders.title: For Rural/Small-Town Readers (Craft + Community Stakes)
ruralReaders.message: Even in a cosmopolitan setting, the heart of the story is hands-on work, reputation, and a business that must survive. The artisan shop, mentorship, and ‘prove yourself’ trial translate to any community where craft and character matter.

sampleCopy.backCoverBlurb:
Calista thought inheriting her family’s gemstone business would mean long hours, tough negotiations, and a few bruised dreams.

She didn’t expect an emerald trial that could ruin her name—or a mysterious Consultant who insists the real danger isn’t the market, but the realm he calls LEGACY.

In a canal-side European town, among velvet trays of stones and the quiet tyranny of craftsmanship, Calista must prove she can source what others can’t, satisfy master jewellers who miss nothing, and decide what she’s willing to trade for excellence.

As the Consultant narrates her ordeal with wry candor, he discovers that guiding her through LEGACY’s levels may cost him more than his pride: it may kill the life he’s been living—or renew it.

Told over three nights and framed as 100 lessons on leadership and inheritance, Calista’s Paradox is a magical-realist fable about ethics, ambition, and the moment you realize legacy is both gift and trap.

socialMediaPosts.text:

Calista’s Paradox is a magical-realist leadership fable told in three nights, framed as 100 lessons on legacy.

A story told in three nights.
A life measured in 100 lessons.
A realm called LEGACY where the cost of learning can be mortal.

Calista’s Paradox—upmarket, wry, and quietly haunting.

Midlife. Two divorces. No kids. A career that suddenly feels like a hallway with no doors.

Then he meets Calista—and becomes her guide through LEGACY.

Calista’s Paradox is for readers who like fiction that makes you think.

One accident. One phone call. One stone that isn’t good enough.

In Calista’s Paradox, small moments trigger life-changing consequences—like a butterfly effect you can’t unsee.
